title: Fix the reference ray occlusion residual and give it an analytic Jacobian; keep explicit seeds with a zero coordinate
body: Four commits on `main` at 78877eaf3. Two are corrections, one replaces a numeric derivative with an analytic one, and one adds a test. The correction to the ray cost removes an early stop; it does not claim better surfaces, and this PR makes no recommendation on `reference_ray_weight`. ### What the commits do, in order 1. **V02, `vc_grow_seg_from_seed`: keep an explicit seed with a zero coordinate.** The explicit seed test joined its three coordinate tests with `&&`, so `-s 0 3936 830` was dropped without a word and the run fell through to `random_seed`. The test now asks for any nonzero coordinate. A seed of `0 0 0` is still read as no seed, since `origin` starts at zero; when one was given on the command line the run now says so in one log line before it picks a random seed. Measured on PHerc1447 with `-s 0 3936 830` (the log line for `0 0 0` is new in this PR and was not part of that build): | build | mode in meta.json | seed in meta.json | |---|---|---| | unchanged | `random_seed` | 2277.850341796875, 5527.7314453125, 3265.960693359375 | | corrected | `explicit_seed` | 0.0, 3936.0, 830.0 | 2. **V01, `GrowPatch`: fix the sign of the reference ray occlusion residual.** `ReferenceRayOcclusionCost` returned `weight * max(0, threshold - max_value)` after a hit. `max_value` is raised to the hit sample before the loop breaks, so on every path that reaches that line `max_value >= threshold` and the residual was zero; the other exit returns zero explicitly. The residual is now `weight * max(0, max_value - threshold)`, the amount by which the first sample at or above the threshold exceeds it. 3. **`GrowPatch`: an analytic Jacobian for that cost.** `NumericDiffCostFunction` marches the ray seven times per evaluation. `ReferenceRayOcclusionAnalyticCost` marches it once with the same arithmetic in the same order, so the residual is the same double. After a hit at the k-th of the n + 1 steps the Jacobian is `weight * (1 - k / (n + 1)) * grad v`, with `grad v` from the trilinear interpolator evaluated once on `ceres::Jet` at the hit point. `ReferenceRayOcclusionCost` is kept as the reference the new cost is tested against. The PR carries only the cost; the instrument we used to compare the two (below) is not in it. 4. **A doctest, `test_reference_ray_occlusion_cost`.** The two ray costs move unchanged to `core/src/ReferenceRayOcclusionCost.hpp`. On a 64^3 volume with one tilted occluding slab it checks that a ray crossing the slab has a positive residual and a ray beside it a zero one, that the analytic cost returns the functor's residual bit for bit, and that its Jacobian matches central differences within 1e-6 of the gradient's largest component on 1,000 random rays whose march does not change between the two probes. On the branch it passes (1,000 of 1,001 rays accepted, residual bits differ on 0, entries over 1e-6: 0). With V01's line reverted it fails on two checks, `REQUIRE(crossing > 0.0)` and `REQUIRE(residual_bits_differ == 0)`. villa's `ctest` passes 184 of 184 on `main` and 185 of 185 on the branch, the difference being the new test. ### The residual and the Jacobian inside a real trace An instrumented copy of the branch logs, at each evaluation during a trace, the numeric functor under central differences and the analytic cost on the same point: 50,000 evaluations on each of three seeds of PHerc1447 (seeded, one thread), 150,000 in all. The residual bits are equal on every row. Each Jacobian entry is put in one class: smooth (judged by |J_analytic − J_numeric| / |J_numeric| ≤ 1e-6), kink (judged against the two one sided slopes, min(|J − s+|, |J − s−|) / max(1, |J|) ≤ 1e-6), jump (the march changes between the two probes, so central differences have no meaning there; counted) and zero (counted). The kink and jump classes were defined after the first comparison had been run. | seed | evaluations | residual bits differ | smooth entries | over 1e-6 | largest relative | kink entries | over 1e-6 | largest | jump | zero | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | seed11 | 50,000 | 0 | 1,305 | 0 | 1.0009864587247572e-07 | 6 | 0 | 0.0 | 531 | 148,158 | | seed26 | 50,000 | 0 | 79,149 | 0 | 4.2656392011281373e-07 | 291 | 0 | 2.384598758003271e-08 | 14,046 | 56,514 | | seed01 | 50,000 | 0 | 105,602 | 0 | 9.740549256703823e-07 | 660 | 0 | 2.4892479604743404e-08 | 15,490 | 28,248 | ### The clock Seed26 of PHerc1447 at 30 generations, seeded, one thread, `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1`, a reference surface set and `reference_ray_weight` 0.5. Cores busy is read from `/proc/stat` over each run, all 24 cores, the run itself included. | build | ray cost | wall seconds | cores busy | when | |---|---|---|---|---| | `main` as shipped (78877eaf3) | residual zero, numeric derivative | 16.76, 16.56, 16.51 | 1.12, 1.09, 1.14 | 2026-09-24, 10:19 to 10:20Z, other jobs on the machine stopped | | V01 alone (our build of 23 September) | live, numeric derivative | median 265.23, range 259.07 to 273.50 | 1.06 to 1.46 | 2026-09-23, 23:18 to 23:44Z | | V01 with the analytic Jacobian (our build of 23 September) | live, analytic Jacobian | median 12.67, range 12.59 to 12.68 | 1.07 to 1.11 | 2026-09-23, 23:18 to 23:44Z | | this branch | live, analytic Jacobian | 12.87, 12.63, 13.50 | 1.11, 1.23, 1.14 | 2026-09-24, 10:19 to 10:20Z, other jobs on the machine stopped | V01 alone costs seven to twenty three times, per seed, in the table below; the Jacobian brings the tracer back to main's speed or better. The branch rows are the check that the branch as built reproduces the build we timed on 23 September: all three write the same `x.tif` (sha256 head 325871f913b8b6c7) as that build's three runs; one of the three times (12.63 s) lies inside that build's range and two (12.87 and 13.50 s) sit above it. The factor of V01 alone over V01 with the analytic Jacobian, per seed, median over median of three runs each, the ranges apart on every seed: | seed | V01 alone, s | V01 with the Jacobian, s | factor | |---|---|---|---| | seed11 | 191.13 (190.51 to 195.86) | 26.76 (26.72 to 27.01) | 7.1424 | | seed26 | 265.23 (259.07 to 273.50) | 12.67 (12.59 to 12.68) | 20.9337 | | seed01 | 279.16 (271.57 to 291.23) | 11.90 (11.77 to 12.49) | 23.4588 | On every seed both arms fill 3,364 cells at 30 generations, and within each arm the three runs write the same `x.tif`; between the numeric and the analytic arm the `x.tif` bytes differ. ### What V01 does to surfaces With the residual at zero the traces below stopped at generation 130 to 185 of the 320 declared; with the sign corrected all three reached generation 320 and wrote every cell of the lattice (407,044). Traces on PHerc1447 at 320 generations, `reference_ray_weight` 0.5, a reference surface grown first from the same seed, seeded, one thread; before is `main`'s residual, after is V01. The three seeds are those whose seed lies in scanned material (at most half of the voxels of the prediction chunk holding the seed are 255, and the raw masked scan there exists and is not 0); six other seeds we ran sit in blocks where the scan has no data and are not counted. The measures are ours: the side of the largest hole free square on cells that lie within one voxel of the prediction's marked surface and that our winding certificate accepts; the edges that certificate refuses by its radial test (a step between neighbours larger than half the winding pitch) and by its angular test (over 20 degrees); and the share of cells within one voxel of the marked prediction. | seed | arm | generation reached | cells | square on marked prediction, mm | radial refused edges (share) | angular refused edges | covered share at 1 voxel | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | seed01 | before | 185 | 135,422 | 2.5956 | 192,924 (0.714248) | 28 | 0.294251 | | seed01 | after | 320 | 407,044 | 0.8779 | 627,017 (0.771421) | 732 | 0.293602 | | seed26 | before | 130 | 66,561 | 2.5988 | 66,240 (0.499525) | 0 | 0.328090 | | seed26 | after | 320 | 407,044 | 0.7002 | 630,166 (0.775291) | 0 | 0.313467 | | seed15 | before | 165 | 107,580 | 3.8133 | 142,200 (0.662925) | 48 | 0.336596 | | seed15 | after | 320 | 407,044 | 0.5364 | 611,398 (0.752201) | 8,084 | 0.424868 | By the measures of this laboratory, with the cost live the square on the marked prediction fell on all three seeds, the edges the winding certificate's radial test refuses grew on all three and those its angular test refuses grew on seed01 and seed15 and stayed at 0 on seed26, and the covered share at one voxel rose on seed15 (0.336596 to 0.424868) and fell on seed01 (0.294251 to 0.293602) and on seed26 (0.328090 to 0.313467). V01 on PHerc. 1447, one slice of the raw scan with the surface before and after. The raw masked scan of PHerc. 1447 at z = 12408, read at level 2 of the published pyramid (one pixel for 4 voxels on a side, grey 37 to 157 mapped to black and white). On it, the surface grown from seed26 cut at the same z: left, the 468 crossings of the surface grown before the correction; right, the 1,948 crossings of the surface grown after it. Each dot is a point where one edge of the surface's lattice crosses the slice. Black is where the scan reads zero, masked away: 134 of the before crossings and 0 of the after crossings lie there. Parameters as in the clock section, at 320 generations. The certificate is not calibrated at this lattice step: on three published segments (PHerc0139 w035 and w040, PHerc1447 z_dbg_gen_00320) its radial test refuses 0.336147 to 0.405866 of the edges. The same runs on a second scroll, PHerc0139, are in progress; their table follows as a comment on this PR when they end. ### Where the cost is on by default `apps/VC3D/elements/JsonProfilePresets.hpp` line 85 at the base, `defaultCopyTracerParamsJson()`, ships `"reference_ray_weight": 0.5`, but the copy flow never sets `reference_surface` (the only setter is `GrowPatch.cpp` line 3374, from a params key that no shipped flow writes), so `reference_raycast_enabled()` is false there and the cost never executes in the copy tracer as shipped: we reproduced the copy flow through `vc_grow_seg_from_seed` on a crop of PHerc0139 w035 and the surface is byte identical with weight 0.5, with weight 0 and on this branch. The cost runs only for a user who sets `reference_surface` in the params JSON, with a positive weight. So V01 and the Jacobian change no shipped flow. We make no recommendation on the weight. ### Prior art We found none for these fixes on villa (searches for the ray occlusion cost, the explicit seed test and `GrowPatch` determinism). The measurements follow two existing items: #1317, which shows that `VC_GROWPATCH_RNG_SEED` with one thread gives byte identical `x/y/z.tif` across runs, and #1795, which caps the OpenBLAS thread pool of `vc_grow_seg_from_seed`; every run here sets `VC_GROWPATCH_RNG_SEED`, one thread and `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1`. This PR carries no check of the seed against the scan: #1877 does that and is the complement for seeds. ### How to reproduce The test, from the repository root: ```bash cmake -S volume-cartographer -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON -DVC_BUILD_FLATBOI=OFF -DVC_TESTING=ON cmake --build build --target test_reference_ray_occlusion_cost -j 4 (cd build && ctest -R test_reference_ray_occlusion_cost --output-on-failure) ``` The clock, on the PHerc1447 surface prediction `20250521151220-surface-20260413222639-surface-m7-L0-th0.2.zarr` (level 0, from `s3://vesuvius-challenge-open-data/PHerc1447/representations/predictions/surfaces/`), with `ref` a surface traced first from the same seed with the same parameters and no reference: ```bash cat > params.json <<'EOF' {"thread_limit": 1, "generations": 30, "step_size": 20, "voxelsize": 8.64, "min_area_cm": 0.0, "cache_size": 8000000000.0, "use_cuda": false, "reference_surface": "ref", "reference_ray_weight": 0.5} EOF VC_GROWPATCH_RNG_SEED=20260923 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 \ /usr/bin/time -f '%e s' vc_grow_seg_from_seed -v surface-m7.zarr -t out -p params.json -s 2464 2411 12410 ```
